## Validation, costs and timing {#validation}

### Do the answers react to the right things?

To see what the answers depend on, we took 10 personas per state with a 2026
governor's race (360 personas in total) and asked them again with one detail
of the prompt changed. To establish a baseline, we also asked the identical
question a second time, which changed 3.9% to 4.7% of governor votes
(@tbl-validation). The most impactful change came from removing the persona's
party, which changed 16% to 20% of votes (four to five times the baseline),
and party-line voting fell from 97% to 80%. Removing party labels from the
candidates changed 5% to 12% of votes, with the greatest movement in Mistral's
responses. Reversing the candidate order or hiding the incumbent label altered
3% to 7% of votes, similar to the baseline, and every persona was able to
identify their own state when asked. Our experiments show that the models
barely react to ballot position, and their responses mostly follow the
persona's party. Argyle et al. [-@argyle2023] found that models conditioned on
a person's background reproduce how groups vote, and Wang et al. [-@wang2025]
found that they also make members of a group more alike than they are. Our
party-drop result shows both, and it fits the AI surveys spreading the states
too far apart: in our AI surveys, a persona's party appears to decide its vote
more often than it does for real voters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-validation
#| tbl-cap: "Share of governor votes that changed when one thing in the prompt was changed, for the 360 validation personas (10 per state), first full run. The top row is the baseline: the identical question asked again."
P.tbl_validation()
```

### Do the answers hold from one day to the next?

Synthetic answers can drift with small changes to wording or timing, as Bisbee
et al. [-@bisbee2024] found. We asked the models the same Method B, Method C
and validation questions over six days: the full run on 25 October, followed
by daily GitHub Actions runs from 28 October to 1 November (@tbl-stability).
On all measures, Mistral was the least stable model. Between days, a race's
margin in Method B shifted by 3.8 points for Mistral, 2.1 for DeepSeek and 1.4
for GPT-6 Luna. Method C was more consistent, moving 0.7 to 1.5 points between
days, and 4% to 8% of the validation personas' votes differed from the first
run. The Method B shifts are slightly smaller than the spread between repeats
on the same day, so most of the movement comes from the models' own
randomness rather than a change over time, and all of it is small next to the
7.2-point gap between the AI surveys and the polls.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-stability
#| tbl-cap: "Day-to-day stability. Spread within a day is the standard deviation across repeats asked the same day; spread between days is the standard deviation of the daily averages; both are in points and averaged over the 36 races."
P.tbl_stability()
```

### Costs and timing

The 67,934 model calls over the six-day period cost US$3.55 in total
(@tbl-costs, @tbl-cost-day). Of that, $2.39 was for the full run on 25
October, when we asked every method. Method A on its own made 32,440 calls and
took 107 minutes to complete, with eight calls running at a time. On the other
days we re-ran Methods B and C with the validation checks, and each of those
runs took about 14 minutes and cost about $0.23. By model, GPT-6 Luna cost
$1.95, because its reasoning tokens are billed as output, DeepSeek $1.18 and
Mistral $0.43. By method, A cost $1.61, B $1.27, the validation checks $0.58
and C $0.10. The GitHub schedule was set for 10:23, but the job usually
started about five hours late, which made no difference to a daily forecast.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-costs
#| tbl-cap: "Every model call to date, by method and model: tokens, average seconds per call and cost in US dollars, as billed by OpenRouter. Seconds per call is the time for one answer; calls ran eight at a time."
P.tbl_costs()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cost-day
#| tbl-cap: "Calls and cost by day. The full run on 25 October asked every method; each daily run re-asks Methods B, C and the validation checks."
P.tbl_cost_by_day()
```
